# Phase One — Chesed Brainstorm: Make Every Mobile Surface Inviting

The Awtsmoos creates the reader, the tree, the composer, and the social road anew;
Awtsmoos.com should greet the thumb with one clear deed, while deeper instruments wait for the user to choose.

## Screenshot wounds that must become durable contracts
- The Heichel/post reader can render raw server exception text instead of Torah content.
- Heichel tree cards consume too much vertical space and expose advanced platform controls over content.
- Social composer overlays a large Review/Publish command slab over the writing canvas.
- Composer shows too many format/media/creator-detail choices simultaneously on a narrow phone.
- Social Hub production still shows the old expanded identity/context stack and large discovery controls.
- The advanced tool affordance can overlap meaningful content.
- Multiple mobile docks use different spacing, elevation, labels, and interruption patterns.
- Blank/fallback/loading states are not consistently inviting or actionable.

## Twenty possible improvements
1. Repair dynamic reader template composition before styling.
2. Add a reader-template regression test that executes the real composition contract.
3. Render a calm reader recovery state instead of raw stack traces if data fails.
4. Make the reader content itself the first visible surface.
5. Collapse reader utilities behind one compact tools disclosure.
6. Keep reading controls below or beside content rather than over it.
7. Reduce Heichel series-card vertical padding and metadata chrome.
8. Keep one primary card action visible and move secondary actions into overflow.
9. Make platform/advanced tools a true closed disclosure on mobile.
10. Prevent advanced panels from floating over the bottom dock.
11. Preserve current Heichel mobile-first work rather than overwrite it.
12. Make composer identity a compact row, not a large card.
13. Make Post/Photo/Video mode selection a compact segmented control.
14. Put advanced media formats behind one disclosure.
15. Put creator details behind one disclosure.
16. Replace the giant sticky publish slab with a compact bottom action bar.
17. Ensure the bottom action bar never covers editable content.
18. Share mobile safe-area and dock clearance tokens across surfaces where practical.
19. Keep motion/glass subtle and never animate blur.
20. Verify every affected route at 390px and 320px with real Chrome.

The Awtsmoos is not hidden by simplicity; simplicity removes the false walls that hide the deed.
